issue.title: Stop a stale callback stat from forcing constant Dag file reparsing

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Once a Dag-level callback has run for a file, the Dag processor reparses that file on
every loop and stops honouring `[dag_processor] min_file_process_interval` for it. It
doesn't clear on its own. Restarting the processor fixes it, until the next Dag run
failure.

### Why

`_add_callback_to_queue` is the only place that sets `bundle_version` on a
`DagFileInfo`; the bundle scan leaves it unset. That's deliberate. `bundle_path` is
`compare=False`, so `bundle_version` is the only field keeping a version-pinned callback
distinct from the scan entry. Without it, a pinned callback would parse against the
tracking checkout instead of the version its Dag run used.

The side effect is that one file can hold two `_file_stats` entries.
`prepare_file_queue` collapses them with

```python
file_stats_by_presence_key = {file.presence_key: stat for file, stat in self._file_stats.items()}
```

which keeps whichever went in last. That's the callback entry, since the file must be
parsed before a run can fail.

That entry never gets a timestamp. `process_parse_results` builds a callback-only stat
without `last_finish_time` (deliberately, to avoid disturbing stale-Dag detection) and
`handle_parsing_result` writes it over the entry wholesale, so the value is `None`. It
stays `None`, because every later parse writes to the scan key instead. From then on the
interval check sees a file that has apparently never been parsed, and requeues it every
loop.

It stays invisible in the stats table, because `_log_file_processing_stats` reads
`_file_stats` by exact key. It reports the scan entry's healthy timestamp while the
queue logic reads the callback entry's `None`.

Only versioning-capable bundles hit this. For unversioned requests
`request.bundle_version` is `None` (see #72930), the two keys coincide, and the merge is
correct.

### Fix

Resolve the `presence_key` collapse from the bundle scan's entry and ignore versioned
(callback) entries. A callback run never records a parse, so a versioned stat is only
ever `None` or a timeout stamp that `_kill_timed_out_processors` writes although nothing
was parsed. `prepare_file_queue` and `_sort_by_mtime` share the new
`_resolve_stats_by_presence_key`, and `emit_metrics` uses it too, so a timed-out
callback's `import_errors=1` no longer keeps `dag_processing.import_errors` at 1
(reported by @fahadabdul). #66484's two versioned-stat tests are flipped to expect the
file to be queued. `processed_recently` is left as is and will be removed separately.

This leaves identity and lifecycle alone, so a versioned callback entry still survives
cleanup while the unversioned file is present.

### Reproduction

Local Airflow built from main, sqlite, `GitDagBundle` (versioning on),
`min_file_process_interval = 30`, two Dags: one with a Dag-level `on_failure_callback`
and a task that raises, one control. Measured by polling `dag.last_parsed_time`:

| phase                                   | callback dag  | control dag |
|-----------------------------------------|---------------|-------------|
| baseline, before any callback            | 1 per 30.0s   | 1 per 30.0s |
| after the Dag-level callback fired       | 1 per 0.4s    | 1 per 30.0s |
| after this change, fresh callback fired  | 1 per 30.0s   | 1 per 30.0s |

The third row triggers a fresh failure after the restart. A restart on its own clears
the state, so measuring that alone would prove nothing.

I found this on 3.3.1, where it held a Dag processor at its 1 CPU limit indefinitely.
Two Dag files were reparsing about 43x more often than configured while the other five
in the same bundle sat exactly on interval.

### Tests

The tests produce the callback stat through the code that writes it in production: a
callback-only `handle_parsing_result`, in both insertion orders, and
`_kill_timed_out_processors`, for the interval check, `modified_time` change detection
and the import-error gauge. Each asserts its setup before checking the result.

### Verification run locally

- The new tests and the two flipped ones pass with the change. Against unpatched
  `manager.py` they all fail except the `callback-recorded-first` case, where insertion
  order happens to pick the scan entry.
- `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_manager.py`: 192 passed, 5 skipped
  (postgres-only). 12 tests error at fixture setup in my local env, and the same 12 error
  on unpatched main, so they are unrelated.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean, and so is `mypy` on the changed
  module.

issue.title: Fix #73432: preserve last_finish_time in callback-only DagFileProcessorManager processing

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Fix #73432 — the dag processor can get stuck in an infinite loop after a Dag-level callback runs.

Here's what happens: when a Dag file gets processed in "callback-only" mode (meaning it was triggered by a Dag callback, not a regular scan), `process_parse_results` creates a new `DagFileStat` with `last_finish_time=None`. That stat overwrites the existing one in `_file_stats`, so on the next scan the file looks like it's never been parsed. The scheduler re-queues it, processes it again, creates another stat with `last_finish_time=None`, and the cycle repeats forever.

The fix is to preserve the existing `last_finish_time` when doing callback-only processing. I added a `last_finish_time` parameter to `process_parse_results` — when it's passed (from the existing stat), the `is_callback_only` branch uses it instead of the current `finish_time`. I updated both call sites:

- `handle_parsing_result`: passes `self._file_stats[file].last_finish_time` — this is the main fix for the reported issue
- `process_unparsed_files`: passes `db_stat.last_finish_time` to `DagFileStat.from_db` — this handles the case where a file is already in the DB

I couldn't run the full airflow test suite here (the test environment needs a database and a bunch of infra), but I did validate the Python syntax with `py_compile` and the logic is pretty straightforward — it's just passing a timestamp through instead of dropping it.

issue.title: [v3-4-test] Stop a stale callback stat from forcing constant Dag file reparsing (#73433)

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Backport of #73433 to `v3-4-test`. It carries the `backport-to-v3-4-test` label and the 3.4.0 milestone, but the backport workflow never ran for it after the merge.

A callback leaves a second, never-refreshed stat entry for a Dag file. That entry makes the file look long unparsed, so `min_file_process_interval` stops excluding it and the Dag processor reparses it on every loop until it restarts. Users hit this on 3.3.x in production (see the discussion on #73433).

The cherry-pick of 72628b5c4f applies to `v3-4-test` without conflicts.
